title: Integrating Deloading into Strength and Physique Sports Training Programmes: An International Delphi Consensus Approach
population: Expert strength and physique coaches: 34 in round one, 29 in round two, 21 in round three.
key_findings: Coaches reached consensus on design principles for building deloads into strength and physique programmes.

Proposed consensus definition: a deload is a period of reduced training stress meant to reduce physiological and psychological fatigue, promote recovery and improve readiness for the training that follows.
methods: Three-round online Delphi: open questions analysed thematically into 138 statements, then rated on a four-point scale for agreement.
limitations: Expert opinion and practice, not measured outcomes; panel shrank from 34 to 21 coaches across rounds.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
